slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: Your serve hits the fence after the bounce.

slides.line:
Glass is fine.
The fence is not.

posts.caption:
Bounces in. Clips the fence. Your partner is already celebrating… should they be? 🎾

After the bounce, a serve may touch the glass – but the wire fence ends it. Second serve.

Comment FAIR or FAULT before you swipe 👇

posts.fact_source: Carbon tow designation: K = thousands of filaments per tow (3K, 12K, 18K)

slides.label: Gear
slides.claim: on a racket means 12 kg of carbon.

posts.caption:
3K, 12K, 18K… sounds like a weight class, right? 🏋️

The K counts filaments: 12K = 12,000 carbon fibres twisted into each thread of the weave. More K usually means a stiffer face.

Knew it? Drop a ✅
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: You hit the ball into your own back glass and it flies over the net.

slides.line:
Your own walls
are fair game.

steps.text: Hit into your own back glass

posts.caption:
The panic shot we all play: smash it into your OWN back glass and pray 🙏

Totally legal – as long as the ball then bounces in the opponents' court.

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: You must hit your serve at waist height or lower.

slides.line:
No tennis serves.
Waist height, max.

posts.caption:
Former tennis players, this one's for you 👀

In padel the ball must be at or below your waist when you hit the serve. Bounce it first, then underhand-ish.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento de Juego, Regla 8.1 and Caso 3

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: You are allowed to volley the return of a serve.

slides.line:
The serve must
bounce in your
box first.

posts.caption:
Tempting to step in and volley that soft serve, right? 😏

Nope. The receiver must always let the serve bounce in the box first.

FAIR or FAULT? 👇

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento, La Pala: solid perforated face, no strings

slides.label: Gear
slides.claim: A padel racket has strings, like a tennis racket.

posts.caption:
Your non-padel friends call it a "bat" for a reason 🏓

No strings: a padel racket is a solid, perforated face – foam core inside, carbon or fibreglass outside.

Tag the friend who still calls it a tennis racket 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: If your racket touches the net during a rally, you lose the point.

slides.line:
Net and posts
are off limits.

posts.caption:
That sweet put-away at the net… and your racket brushes the tape 😬

Point gone. Body, racket or anything you carry touching the net or posts while the ball is in play = point lost.

FAIR or FAULT? 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: Your shot hits their back glass before it bounces. You win the point.

slides.line:
It must bounce
on their floor first.

posts.caption:
Full power, straight into their back glass, no bounce. Winner? 💥

Nope – the ball must bounce on the opponents' floor before it touches any of their walls.

FAIR or FAULT? 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

posts.fact_source: FIP Reglamento, La Pala: max length 45.5 cm, width 26 cm, thickness 38 mm

slides.label: Gear
slides.claim: is the maximum length of a padel racket.

posts.caption:
Head + handle together: 45.5 cm, not a millimetre more 📏

And the face may be max 26 cm wide and 38 mm thick.

Did you know the numbers? 👇
Follow @fairorfault – your daily padel quiz.

slides.label: Rules
slides.claim: Your serve touches the net and lands in the box. You serve again.

slides.line:
Net + in = replay.
Unless it then
hits the **fence**.

posts.caption:
Net cord on the serve, ball drops in the box. Fault? 🤔

No – you simply serve again. Only if it then hits the wire fence does it become a fault.
